title: Khadijah dies
hook: Khadijah dies, and in Bukhari's reports he never stops speaking of her

segments.voice: Yesterday, al-sahifa. Your line was: conscience ended it. Did you say your one fair sentence, or find someone to stand with you? Day seven hundred forty-eight.

In Medina, years after the events we're following, a sheep has been slaughtered in the Prophet's household. He cuts it into portions, and sends some out, not to his companions, but to a few women around the city. Aisha, his wife, watches this happen again and again. Who are they? They are the friends of a woman she never met. The boycott is over, and a new part of the story opens, the part of sorrow. It opens with a loss that he carried for the rest of his life. Today: Khadijah dies.
screen: `A SHEEP, CUT INTO PORTIONS.` → `SENT TO OLD FRIENDS.` → `WHOSE FRIENDS?`

segments.voice: Khadijah was the one he ran home to when the revelation began, the one who wrapped him up and said that God would never disgrace him. She was his wife and his shelter, and, as the sirah tells it, she stood beside him through the hungry years in the valley. Then, after the boycott, she dies. The sources are short about the death itself. What they keep, at length, is what came after. Aisha, in Sahih al-Bukhari, is frank about it. She says she was never jealous of any woman the way she was of Khadijah, though she had never seen her, because the Prophet mentioned her so often. And that detail of the sheep, the portions sent to Khadijah's friends, comes from the same report. Another report in Bukhari is even smaller and even more telling. Khadijah's sister, Hala, comes to the door one day and asks permission to come in. Something in the way she asks, her voice, her manner, is like Khadijah's. And he is shaken by it, and calls out, O Allah, Hala. Years after her death, a voice at the door could still do that. In Sahih Muslim he puts it in his own words: he was given her love. Not that he chose it, or earned it. It was given. And Bukhari also reports that Jibril told him to give Khadijah good news of a house in Paradise, a place with no noise in it and no tiredness. Hold those together. The grief is real. The love is called a gift. And the memory shows up in ordinary things: meat for her friends, a sister's knock.
screen: `THE ONE HE RAN HOME TO.` · `AISHA: NEVER SO JEALOUS.` · `A SISTER'S VOICE AT THE DOOR.` · `HER LOVE WAS GIVEN TO HIM.` · then, large: `MEAT FOR HER FRIENDS.`

segments.voice: The practice: speak of someone you've lost. Sit, and let your shoulders drop. Bring to mind one person who is gone. It may be a recent loss, or an old one. Let one ordinary detail come back: a voice, a phrase they used, a dish they made, the way they knocked. Stay with it. Then, if you can, say their name out loud, quietly. Say one thing they did that you're glad of. If you pray, you can ask Allah's mercy for them, the way Muslims do for those who have died. If it's too heavy today, just their name is enough. The bell holds the time.
Khadijah dies. And in the hadith, she is still in his speech long after: her friends fed, her sister's voice recognized, her love called a gift. Today's word.
Your line: he never forgot her. Today, tell one person a small story about someone you've lost, or do one small thing for someone they loved. Day seven hundred forty-eight.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Khadijah as a Mother of the Believers; her life and the Prophet's love for her are retold in sirah study, and Muslims pray for mercy on those who have died.

pairs: a voice at the door like her sister's
good news of a house in Paradise

myth: she says she never saw her; she knew her through how often he spoke of her.
he sent meat to Khadijah's friends after her death
Aisha reports it in Sahih al-Bukhari.
in Sahih Muslim he says he was given her love
love described as a gift, not an achievement.

fork.setup: you're in his house years later. a woman at the door asks to come in, and her voice sounds like someone long gone. what happens?
options: he's shaken, and calls out Hala's name.
he asks her to come back another day.
fork.reveal: Bukhari reports that Hala's way of asking reminded him of Khadijah; he was shaken, and said: O Allah, Hala.

original.note: Arabic: the name of the Prophet's wife Khadijah bint Khuwaylid.

trapdoor: what you thought: a death reported in a line.
what it means: a loss he carried, remembered in small, ordinary acts.
what a scholar hears: Aisha's reports in Bukhari (the sheep, Hala at the door), Muslim's 'I was given her love', and the house in Paradise.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3818 (Aisha: never so jealous of any woman; he mentioned her often; sent portions of a slaughtered sheep to her friends)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3820 (Jibril: give Khadijah good news of a house in Paradise, with no noise and no toil)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3821 (Hala bint Khuwaylid asks permission to enter; he recognizes Khadijah's way of asking)
Sahih Muslim 2435 (he was given, or nourished with, her love)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3 (Khadijah comforts him after the first revelation: Allah will never disgrace you)
Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (Khadijah's death after the boycott; her support of him)
